text:
anya: Heads up — canary rollout for interregion mesh (us->eu) started at 08:12 UTC and we saw ~5% mTLS handshake failures starting ~08:13. Correlated with keystore role churn. Opening thread for quick triage + fallback runbook.

ben: Saw the same. Proxy logs show TLS handshake error:
```json
{"error":"tls: client authentication failed: unknown certificate","proxy":"svc-mesh-proxy-2","ts":"2026-03-21T08:13:07Z"}
```
Also found KMS decrypt denies in keystore: 
```json
{"error":"AccessDenied","requestId":"req-0a1b2c3d","principal":"infra-ci@redwood"}
```

leo: We rolled an RBAC change earlier in the window — PR  https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4789 removed a member from clusterrolebinding `keystore-readers` in eu by mistake. Oops.

maria: Who approved that PR? We need audit log IDs for the RBAC change + KMS requestIds to correlate. If it was manual, we should treat this as a vuln/ops gap.

anya: Proposed quick runbook (short):
1) Re-add the removed member to `keystore-readers` in eu (temp fix).
2) Force keystore service to refresh any cached credentials and kv cache on proxies.
3) If KMS denies persist, create a short-lived allow grant and collect KMS request IDs.
4) Monitor mTLS handshake rate + error budget for 30m.
5) Create incident ticket and start postmortem if failures >1%.

ben: I'm +1 on that. I'll prepare a temporary KMS grant and the rebind. Example AWS CLI grant command (we use multi-cloud but this is the pattern):
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/keystore-eu --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/infra-keystore-reader --operations Decrypt --name "temp-keystore-debug"
```
I'll post the grant id once created.

leo: For cache evict on proxies, call the keystore admin endpoint (internal):
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://keystore.eu.internal/api/v1/cache/evict -d '{"scope":"proxy-kv"}'
```
That should force new cert fetches.

keystore-bot: config-watcher detected RBAC change at 08:09 UTC: clusterrolebinding `keystore-readers` diff -> member `infra-ci@redwood` removed (actor: leo). Rule: flagged as manual change without `rbac/approved` tag.

maria: Add this to incidents channel and notify compliance. We need to capture who merged and why there was no approval tag. Also ensure KMS audit logs are retained for 90 days for this key.

anya: I'll re-add the member and kick the cache refresh now. Ben, please post the KMS grant id and grant status here once done. We'll watch handshake rate for the next 30m and roll back if anything odd.

ben: On it — creating grant now, will update in ~2m.

leo: Adding a follow-up action: create an automated guardrail so any RBAC change touching `keystore-*` roles requires a 2nd approver and auto-annotates the PR with `rbac/approved-by`. I'll draft the policy.

maria: Also recommend adding an alert rule: if KMS Decrypt AccessDenied spikes by >3 within 5m for keystore key, page eng-oncall.

anya: Good. I'll open incident and start the postmortem template. Thanks all.

ben: Grant created: id g-9a8b7c6d, applied to role/infra-keystore-reader. KMS logs show successful Decrypts now. Monitoring shows handshake errors dropping to ~0.2%.

anya: Thanks — closing triage here, moving to incident for follow-up items (RBAC guardrail, audit retention, postmortem).
